Development USB diagnostics. Direct USB playback is not implemented. Stop music before the Session 5 forced ownership experiment.

Session 7 development diagnostic: stop normal playback. This force-owns the USB audio interfaces and sends a real direct USB stream of DIGITAL SILENCE ONLY. No audible tone should be produced. For the first run, use a conservative DAC volume and keep IEMs out of your ears initially: interface transitions may produce a transient. The test stops automatically after about one second, then restores USB configuration. A physical DAC reconnect may be required afterward. Copy the report before reconnecting; do not immediately repeat. This is diagnostics, not a Bit-perfect playback mode.
Target: PCM16 signed LE, stereo, 44100 Hz; digital zero only

Session 6 development test: stop all Sazanami playback first. This temporarily takes AudioControl and AudioStreaming from Android, programs the DAC clock to 44.1 kHz and selects stereo PCM16. NO music or audio data is sent. It establishes and restores the descriptor-resolved idle alternate and the original clock, then releases AS before AC. Normal Android USB routing may stop working afterward; the tested KA15/Samsung environment has required physical reconnect after forced ownership.

After this configuration experiment, physically disconnect/reconnect the DAC if normal Android playback routes incorrectly or the DAC behaves abnormally. Kernel bindings and framework enumeration do not verify functional USB audio recovery.
Testing forced AC ownership and recovery…
Functional USB audio playback: NOT VERIFIED

Development warning: kernel bindings and Android USB enumeration do not verify usable audio routing or DAC playback. If audio routes to the phone speaker or the DAC behaves abnormally, physically disconnect and reconnect the DAC before continuing.

Known manual KA15/Samsung test evidence, not automatically detected: repeated forced AudioControl ownership left playback on the phone speaker despite restored enumeration. Physical disconnect/reconnect restored DAC playback. This was observed in that environment; it is not a universal rule for USB DACs. HID controls working does not prove audio playback works.

Session 5: stop all music first. This temporarily detaches Android’s USB-audio driver from AudioControl; the DAC may disappear from Android audio routing. No USB audio data is sent. AudioControl is released immediately after the clock reads, then recovery is observed for up to 2 seconds. Run Inspect kernel USB ownership first.
Playback service is unavailable. Reopen Sazanami and wait for playback to connect.
USB audio report copied, including raw descriptor evidence.
Diagnostic experiment: temporary AudioControl ownership with force=false, read-only clock queries, then release. No USB playback.
Diagnostic only: kernel drivers, actual USB speed, one non-forced AudioControl claim with immediate release, and Android USB output capabilities. No driver detach or playback.

Session 8 development diagnostic: intentional AUDIBLE direct-USB PCM with a LOW-LEVEL signal. Stop normal Sazanami playback completely. LOWER DAC volume substantially before the first test; do not use normal/high listening volume. Expected: brief LEFT tone, pause, brief RIGHT tone. Automatic stop after approximately one second. A physical DAC reconnect may be required afterward. Copy the complete report before reconnecting; do not immediately repeat. This is not normal music playback.
PCM16 signed LE stereo, 44100 Hz; fixed 441 Hz reference, peak ±1024; LEFT → silence → RIGHT

Bounded FLAC direct USB transport — Session 10
Play FLAC directly over USB (5 s)

Stop normal playback first. Real music can reach full scale: lower KA15 volume from your usual 60A to about 15A–20A for the first run. Do not raise volume during that run, even if quiet. Wait for automatic stop; do not immediately repeat. Copy the complete report before reconnecting.

Restoration=%1$s; AS release=%2$s; AC release=%3$s; original FLAC fd closed=%4$s

Native FLAC only: 44100 Hz / stereo / 16-bit, starting at frame 0. Whole-file MD5: NOT APPLICABLE — bounded prefix. Expected: about five seconds of the selected track. Listening, DAC display and normal playback recovery require manual observation. Production Bit-perfect playback and normal player integration remain unimplemented.
Full FLAC direct USB transport — Session 11
Play full FLAC directly over USB

Stop normal playback first. Keep KA15 physical volume around 15A–20A for the first run. This plays one whole supported track at its original amplitude. Let it end naturally, or use Stop to abort safely. Do not immediately repeat; copy the complete report before reconnecting.

Native FLAC only: 44100 Hz / stereo / 16-bit, from frame 0 to verified natural EOF. Whole-file MD5 and every source frame must verify. No pause, seek, next track, normal-player integration or production Bit-perfect mode. Listening and recovery require manual observation.
